conventions.convention: The Heisenberg multiplication is (v,t)(w,s)=(v+w,t+s−ω(v,w)/2), and the central character is exp(iλt).
W(v)W(w)=exp(−iλω(v,w)/2)W(v+w); regularity means strong continuity of t↦W(tv) for every v. The Hilbert space is nonzero, and irreducibility concerns closed invariant subspaces.
The universal Weyl algebra treats the additive phase space as discrete and imposes no continuity on its unitary generators. Its construction assumes Countable Choice.
Incomplete tensor products use H₀=ℂ, Hₙ=L²(ℝⁿ), and embeddings that append copies of a fixed unit reference vector. Coordinates are indexed by j≥1.
Finite-dimensional uniqueness assumes AC and a fixed nonzero real parameter λ; the zero-dimensional phase space is included.
The infinite-mode example uses only finitely supported phase-space vectors, parameter λ=1, and the two reference Gaussians with a=1,2. Regularity is asserted on each real line.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For n≥0 and λ≠0, Sλ(q,p,t)f(x)=exp(iλt+iλp·(x−q/2))f(x−q) is a strongly continuous unitary Heisenberg representation with central character exp(iλt), and its Weyl operators form an irreducible regular Weyl system with phase exp(−iλω/2).

The finite-dimensional Heisenberg group is second-countable locally compact and is N⋊αK, with αq(p,t)=(p,t−q·p). For λ≠0, the dual action is free and transitive on the characters χa,λ(p,t)=exp(i(a·p+λt)), and q↦χλq,λ identifies K with this orbit.

Under Countable Choice, the twisted finite-support algebra is a unital *-algebra, the displayed universal supremum is a finite nonzero C*-seminorm, and its kernel quotient completion is universal for the displayed unitary Weyl relations. Every unital *-representation of the algebraic relations extends uniquely to a bounded *-representation of the completion.

Assume Countable Choice. For a>0, the normalized Gaussian-weighted average of the one-mode Schrödinger Weyl operators is the orthogonal projection onto Ωa(x)=(a/π)^(1/4)exp(−ax²/2). Its Weyl orbit has dense span; bounded intertwiners intertwine the corresponding averages, and coordinate averages act as the local rank-one projections in incomplete tensor products.

Assume Countable Choice. The incomplete tensor product with unit reference vector Ω is the Hilbert completion of the compatible union of L²(ℝⁿ) under embeddings appending Ω factors; every coordinate rank-one projection onto a unit vector Φ extends to an orthogonal projection on that completion.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system on a finite-dimensional real symplectic space of dimension 2n, with fixed λ≠0 and phase exp(−iλω/2), is unitarily equivalent to Wλ(q,p)f(x)=exp(iλp·(x−q/2))f(x−q) on L²(ℝⁿ).

concerns.concern: Steps 3.1–4.1 classify the characters and then treat their parameters as Euclidean topological coordinates: step 4.1 says the orbit map is continuous with continuous inverse. The cited real-line character lemma proves the character classification, but does not establish that the parameter map ℝ→ℝ-hat is a homeomorphism for the compact-open topology; the finite-product dual lemma does not supply this missing one-factor assertion. This is a short gap: bounded-interval uniform estimates prove forward continuity, and uniform closeness to 1 on [−1,1] forces the frequency parameter to be small, proving inverse continuity. The downstream uniqueness proof uses this orbit identification as a Borel isomorphism in step 4.1.
